core_obligations: Use the functorial splitting of the map from C(N tensor_R S) to C(N) to build the upper vertical arrows of a three-by-three commutative diagram whose column composites are identities (proof lines 1448-1473).
Read off the dashed arrow from the second row being a coequalizer diagram, and deduce from the top right square that the first row is a split coequalizer (proof lines 1474-1479).

Apply the adjunction to tensor with S inside C, obtaining the split coequalizer diagram relating the triple tensor product, the double tensor product and f_*(M, theta) tensor_R S (proof lines 1480-1490).
Conclude by faithfulness of C that the diagram of the lemma is an equalizer (proof lines 1491-1493).
proof_roadmap: Functorial splitting and the three-by-three diagram (proof lines 1448-1473).
Dashed arrow and the split coequalizer (proof lines 1474-1479).
Tensoring inside C by the adjunction (proof lines 1480-1490).
difficulty_reason: In the setting of a ring map R to S together with the two projections from S to S tensor_R S and the three from S to the triple tensor product, the lemma states that if f: N to M is universally injective then the diagram obtained by tensoring the equalizer diagram of f with S over R is again an equalizer (statement lines 1429-1445). The proof is an explicit diagram chase of real substance: the author first splits the map C(N tensor_R S) to C(N) functorially in N, which produces the upper vertical arrows of a three-by-three commutative diagram whose column composites are identities, then reads off a dashed arrow because the second row is a coequalizer diagram, and deduces from the top right square that the first row is a split coequalizer (proof lines 1448-1479). Tensoring with S inside the functor C is then justified by the adjunction remark, producing a split coequalizer diagram whose comparison with the desired diagram, together with faithfulness of C, forces the desired diagram to be an equalizer (proof lines 1480-1493). The claim is H3: the split-coequalizer bookkeeping across a three-by-three diagram together with the functorial splitting and the adjunction step is an original assembly, not a citation chain.
